hard_think: A content-addressed component name is not a composition proof; the pair must bind every component descriptor, inventory, tree digest, count, byte total, platform, interpreter row, and dependency role.
Sequential full verification can stale its first result while the second component is read, so a bounded reverse pass and full-binding equality are required for this inert layer.
No finite read-only reproof establishes durable immutability against a concurrent writer; empirical write denial remains a separate principal and lifecycle gate.
The 72,261-file double pass is viable as offline release evidence but cannot scale as interactive query work.

The initial B -> D -> interpreter approach was rejected after the hostile mutation counterexample, despite its passing nominal tests.

Promoting composition directly to route-v2 was rejected because native-loader closure, deterministic effects, pre-import bootstrap, signing, empirical write denial, and exact runtime closure remain false.
first_principles: One inert descriptor may identify an exact verified pair without owning or copying either payload.

Every activation-grade property remains false until its own independently falsifiable gate passes.
Full-tree verification belongs to publication, reuse, release, and promotion boundaries, never the read-only query path.
